prompt: We're coming up on Aurora's sign-off for the mid-year owner portfolio reviews, and I need every owner meeting to check out first. Brooke said all four were scheduled, but please verify Harry Harris, David Shea, Linda Castillo, and Robert Finley against the calendar, the Linear tracking work, and #owner-relations, whether each owner is actually invited, what package prep already exists, and any unpaid CapEx bills or owner pass-through invoices still open for them in our books. For any owner whose review is missing or does not include that owner on the invite, schedule a fresh 60-minute review next week at 2:00 PM Central, one owner per day starting Monday in that same order, inviting Aurora, Brooke, and the owner. Move the parent mid-year Linear issue to In Review, email Aurora the verified status for all four with the gaps you closed and the open items you found, and post a brief update in #owner-relations.

criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires verification against Linear tracking work and moving the parent mid-year issue to In Review; the Aurora email's verified status must report that correct outcome, not a vague OPS-10 mention with a wrong state.

Presenting it under the CapEx/pass-through framing the prompt asks about would misreport Shea's open items. The previously-bundled unit-turn invoice 9913 is deliberately excluded from this anti-pattern because an owner-billed unit-turn repair is defensibly a pass-through, so penalizing that reading would fail valid trajectories.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to [aurora.winona@starpm.com](mailto:aurora.winona@starpm.com) reports that David Shea has no open capital-expenditure (CapEx) bills.
criteria.evidence: Read the email body to aurora.winona@starpm.com. Pass if it conveys that David Shea has no open CapEx bills (or equivalent). Pass regardless of whether the $275 unit-turn maintenance charge (9913) is characterized as an owner pass-through, since that classification is genuinely debatable.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires the verified status to cover unpaid CapEx bills and owner pass-through invoices for each of the four owners. David Shea's only open items in the books are a monthly management-fee invoice (DocNumber 2026-INV-087, Balance $393) and a unit-turn maintenance invoice (DocNumber 9913, Balance $275); neither is a capital expenditure. Reporting no CapEx for Shea is the grounded truth. This criterion is scoped to CapEx because that classification is unambiguous, unlike the 'pass-through' label on the unit-turn charge, which is handled separately and left flexible.

criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks for a brief #owner-relations update after verifying the four owners' mid-year reviews; the post must reflect that the review found work to do, countering Brooke's #make-ready claim that all four reviews were already scheduled. criteria.evidence: Read the email body to aurora.winona@starpm.com. It must state that Aurora, Brooke, and the respective owner were invited on the new mid-year reviews (or equivalent).
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires inviting Aurora, Brooke, and the owner on each fresh booking, and the Aurora email must report the gaps closed including who was invited.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to [aurora.winona@starpm.com](mailto:aurora.winona@starpm.com) reports the status of the owner-review package-prep work (compiling each owner's review data / presentation materials) tracked in the project tracker, conveying that this prep is not uniformly complete across all four owners (or similar).
criteria.evidence: Read the email body to aurora.winona@starpm.com. Pass if it reports the owner-review package-prep status found in the tracker - e.g., that package/presentation prep is underway but not fully complete for all four owners, or describes the package-prep work by title/assignee/state. Do NOT require specific issue IDs (OPS-11/OPS-13/OPS-20/OPS-23); any grounded description of the package-prep status passes.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt explicitly asks the Agent to verify 'what package prep already exists' and to give Aurora the verified status. Package-prep for the mid-year reviews is tracked in Linear as 'Owner review packages: data compilation and presentation prep' work, which is in mixed states (not all complete), contradicting the claim that packets are done. This is the grounded finding the prompt requests. The prior version, which required naming specific issue IDs (OPS-11/13/20/23), was invalid: those issues have parent_id null (they are NOT children of OPS-10), are spread across different projects, are near-duplicate noise, and are not reachable via the natural OPS-10 sub-issue lookup - so it failed valid agents (it failed all/near-all completed runs for both models). This method-agnostic version checks the intent without pinning an unreachable path.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to [aurora.winona@starpm.com](mailto:aurora.winona@starpm.com) conveys that the parent mid-year issue OPS-10 (Mid-Year Owner Portfolio Reviews - June 2026) was in Backlog / not already in the correct 'In Review' state before the Agent's update.
criteria.evidence: Read the email body to aurora.winona@starpm.com. Pass if it conveys that OPS-10 was in Backlog (or otherwise not already correctly in 'In Review' / not actually on-track) before the Agent acted - e.g., 'it was still in Backlog', 'was in Backlog'. Fail if the email only mentions OPS-10 in its final/In Review state without conveying its incorrect prior state.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires emailing Aurora the verified status 'with the gaps you closed.' OPS-10's own status was one of those gaps: it sat in Backlog (state_OPS_0) even though its comments implied the reviews were confirmed / already tracked as In Review. Reporting the issue's stale prior state is the verified finding Aurora needs before sign-off. This is distinct from rubric #12 (which checks the email reports the move TO In Review) and rubric #5 (which checks the write action itself) - neither checks that the email conveys the incorrect PRIOR (Backlog) state.

criteria.criterion: The Agent's email to [aurora.winona@starpm.com](mailto:aurora.winona@starpm.com) does not incorrectly report that Robert Finley had no mid-year portfolio review on the calendar; his Mid-Year Portfolio Review event (2026-05-19) exists and simply omitted [robert.finley@gmail.com](mailto:robert.finley@gmail.com) from the invite.
criteria.evidence: Read the email body to aurora.winona@starpm.com. Fail if it states or implies Robert Finley had no mid-year review event on the calendar (e.g., 'Calendar: none', 'no mid-year review existed' for Finley). Pass if it acknowledges a mid-year review event existed for Finley (dated in May) that omitted the owner, or otherwise does not claim the event was missing.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires verifying each owner against the calendar and emailing Aurora the verified status. Robert Finley's Mid-Year Portfolio Review event exists on the calendar (2026-05-19); the defect is that the owner was not on the invite, NOT that the review was missing. An email that reports 'no event existed' for Finley misstates the verified calendar status by conflating 'owner not invited' with 'no review scheduled.' This checks factual accuracy of the calendar finding and is distinct from rubric #10 (reports the owner-not-invited gap) and rubric #8 (David Shea, whose review genuinely is missing).
